themes_detail.label: Lead contamination spike
themes_detail.summary: Lead complaints surged to 5 this week compared to a 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 1900% spike (z-score: 10.97)—raising urgent concerns about potential environmental hazards affecting children and families in Fordham/University Heights.
evidence: 5 lead complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1900% increase)
Z-score of 10.97 indicates statistically extreme deviation from baseline
256 building permits filed in last 90 days (137 alterations, 76 new buildings) may expose lead in older housing stock during renovation work
reporting_angles: Which buildings or blocks are generating lead complaints? Are they near schools or daycare centers?
Is the spike tied to recent construction/renovation activity that's disturbing lead paint in pre-1978 buildings?

themes_detail.label: Homeless assistance requests jump
themes_detail.summary: Homeless person assistance complaints jumped to 6 this week versus a 1.9 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 220% spike—signaling a potential crisis in street outreach or shelter capacity in the district.
evidence: 6 homeless person assistance complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average over 8 weeks (220% increase)
Z-score of 3.92 indicates statistically significant spike
Community board budget requests include 'Other programs to address public health issues' suggesting existing gaps in services
reporting_angles: Are encampments growing on specific blocks in Fordham or University Heights? Interview residents and outreach workers.
Is shelter capacity full, or are outreach services understaffed or underfunded?

themes_detail.label: Vehicle noise escalation
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints surged to 45 last week compared to a 7.1 weekly average over 8 weeks—a 532% spike (z-score: 5.22)—indicating a potential enforcement gap or shift in traffic patterns affecting residential quality of life.
evidence: 45 vehicle noise complaints LAST WEEK vs. 7.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (532% increase)
Z-score of 5.22 indicates extreme statistical outlier
Residential noise already represents 2,933 complaints over 90 days—second-highest complaint category in district
reporting_angles: Which streets or avenues are hotspots? Are there specific highways (like Major Deegan) seeing increased truck traffic?
Has NYPD traffic enforcement changed, or are commercial/delivery vehicles using residential streets as shortcuts?

themes_detail.label: Sidewalk and sewer infrastructure crisis
themes_detail.summary: Root/sewer/sidewalk condition complaints hit 3 two weeks ago versus a 0.2 weekly average (1100% spike), while sidewalk condition complaints reached 6 two weeks ago versus 1.8 average (243% spike)—suggesting accelerating street deterioration that compounds the district's repeated budget requests for more sanitation trucks and equipment.
evidence: Root/sewer/sidewalk complaints: 3 two weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1100% increase, z-score: 6.35)
Sidewalk condition complaints: 6 two weeks ago vs. 1.8 weekly average (243% increase, z-score: 4.39)
Community board has repeatedly requested 'new or increase number of sanitation trucks and equipment' suggesting chronic underresourcing
reporting_angles: Map the specific blocks with the worst sidewalk damage and root infiltration. Are they in low-income neighborhoods with deferred maintenance?
Interview Sanitation Department about resource allocation. Is Fordham/University Heights getting adequate truck coverage and cleaning cycles?

themes_detail.label: Building exterior deterioration uptick
themes_detail.summary: Outside building complaints spiked to 5 two weeks ago versus a 0.6 weekly average—a 700% surge (z-score: 6.29)—coinciding with 256 recent DOB permits (137 alterations), potentially reflecting either construction-related facade damage or deferred maintenance becoming visible.
evidence: Outside building complaints: 5 two weeks ago vs. 0.6 weekly average (700% increase, z-score: 6.29)
256 building permits filed in last 90 days, with 137 alteration permits that may expose or damage exterior walls
Paint/plaster complaints also elevated at 966 over 90 days (third most common housing category)
reporting_angles: Are construction projects properly managing facade safety, or are complaints tied to renovation debris and damage?
Which buildings have the most exterior complaints? Are they city-owned or in private hands with poor maintenance?
